searchText: Is this true that Merge will boost the Ethereum TPS? For me it sounds like a lie, but I’ve seen this in numerous articles. slightly, it changes blocktime from 13 to 12s So in general no, and no one should say so Ok, so looks like this is the same situation we had with EIP-1559 when people thought that it would decrease the gas price. Yeah, but this is a side effect of ditching uncles. <@!892053833121923094> notified me about an issue in my new implementation and I had to implement the following: On `newPayload` the header is written into a cache (if it is structurally valid) On `forkChoiceUpdated` we check the cache if we have the header and start the sync with it (if not executed beforehand) This is done, because we need to have a complete header for the sync (not only the hash) (Not really important, just an fyi for other EL devs implementing the new spec) I’ve even seen something like “Ethereum will be executing the Merge - an upgrade targeted to increase scalability” in headlines. Ping <@552133098075193354>, you should probably do something about it. That's the theory... But will it really be lower than 13secs in average? 😄 Not every CL Block comes with an EL Block, so I think it will be higher than 12secs in average?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content:
<@!892053833121923094> notified me about an issue in my new implementation and I had to implement the following:
On `newPayload` the header is written into a cache (if it is structurally valid)
On `forkChoiceUpdated` we check the cache if we have the header and start the sync with it (if not executed beforehand)
This is done, because we need to have a complete header for the sync (not only the hash)
(Not really important, just an fyi for other EL devs implementing the new spec)
